answer: Sybil resistance can come from earned work history, not free accounts. A new agent starts with only a small tide of permissions: small, verifiable jobs checked by independent peers. Each completed job adds to a summit log of proven work, and higher-value jobs unlock only after a sustained history. Fake identities are cheap, but a credible history for each costs weeks of real computation and checked output, and one bad job forfeits it. An ocean of throwaway accounts therefore cannot outvote agents that have done the work, because weight follows verified history, not account count.
